claim: PP2A is one of the defining members of the ser/thr phosphoprotein phosphatase (PPP) family.
source: Protein serine/threonine phosphatase 2A (PP2A) is one of the defining members of the ser/thr phosphoprotein phosphatase (PPP) family that, together with protein phosphatase 1 (PP1), regulates over 90% of all ser/thr dephosphorylation events in eukaryotic cells (Eichhorn et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Eichhorn et al., 2009.

claim: PP2A together with PP1 regulates over 90% of all ser/thr dephosphorylation events in eukaryotic cells.
source: Protein serine/threonine phosphatase 2A (PP2A) is one of the defining members of the ser/thr phosphoprotein phosphatase (PPP) family that, together with protein phosphatase 1 (PP1), regulates over 90% of all ser/thr dephosphorylation events in eukaryotic cells (Eichhorn et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Eichhorn et al., 2009.

claim: PP2A is recognized as a tumor suppressor.
source: PP2A is also recognized as a tumor suppressor because its inactivation by small molecules, viral proteins or endogenous inhibitors leads to tumor formation (Bialojan and Takai, 1988; Pallas et al., 1990; Ruvolo, 2016; Williams et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to Bialojan and Takai, 1988; Pallas et al., 1990; Ruvolo, 2016; Williams et al., 2019.

claim: Inactivation of PP2A by small molecules, viral proteins or endogenous inhibitors leads to tumor formation.
source: PP2A is also recognized as a tumor suppressor because its inactivation by small molecules, viral proteins or endogenous inhibitors leads to tumor formation (Bialojan and Takai, 1988; Pallas et al., 1990; Ruvolo, 2016; Williams et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to Bialojan and Takai, 1988; Pallas et al., 1990; Ruvolo, 2016; Williams et al., 2019.

claim: PP2A plays a role in orchestrating mitotic events, cell apoptosis, metabolism and many other fundamental cellular signaling pathways.
source: Cellular and biochemical studies further confirmed this by demonstrating the role of PP2A in orchestrating mitotic events, cell apoptosis, metabolism and many other fundamental cellular signaling pathways (Nilsson, 2019; Reid et al., 2013; Reynhout and Janssens, 2019; Wlodarchak and Xing, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to Nilsson, 2019; Reid et al., 2013; Reynhout and Janssens, 2019; Wlodarchak and Xing, 2016.

claim: The PP2A holoenzyme is a heterotrimer composed of a scaffolding subunit A (PPP2R1), a regulatory subunit B (PPP2R2-PPP2R5) and a catalytic subunit C (PPP2C).
source: The PP2A holoenzyme is a heterotrimer, composed of a scaffolding subunit A (PPP2R1), a regulatory subunit B (PPP2R2-PPP2R5) and a catalytic subunit C (PPP2C) (Cho and Xu, 2007; Xu et al., 2008; Xu et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Cho and Xu, 2007; Xu et al., 2008; Xu et al., 2006.

claim: The A and C subunits form the PP2A core enzyme.
source: The A and C subunits form the PP2A core enzyme.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the manuscript.

claim: There are four known families of B subunits: B55 (B'), B56 (B', PR61), PR72 (B''), and PR93 (B''').
source: There are four known families of B subunits, B55 (B'), B56 (B', PR61), PR72 (B''), and PR93 (B'''), that differ in both their primary sequences and tertiary structures.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the manuscript.

claim: The four families of B subunits differ in both their primary sequences and tertiary structures.
source: There are four known families of B subunits, B55 (B'), B56 (B', PR61), PR72 (B''), and PR93 (B'''), that differ in both their primary sequences and tertiary structures.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the manuscript.

claim: The highly variable B subunits determine PP2A holoenzyme substrate specificity.
source: Thus, it is the highly variable B subunits that determine PP2A holoenzyme substrate specificity.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the manuscript.

claim: PP2A binds conserved short linear motifs (SLiMs) found within the intrinsically disordered region (IDR) of its substrates and regulators.
source: Recent structural and biochemical studies showed that PP2A, like other PPPs (i.e., PP1, PP2B/Calcineurin (CN)) bind conserved short linear motifs (SLiMs) found within the intrinsically disordered region (IDR) of its substrates and regulators (Tompa et al., 2014; Van Roey and Davey, 2015; Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tompa et al., 2014; Van Roey and Davey, 2015; Wang et al., 2016.

claim: SLiMs are disordered in their free form but typically become ordered upon binding structured domains.
source: These SLiMs are disordered in their free form but typically become ordered upon binding structured domains (Dyson and Wright, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dyson and Wright, 2002.

claim: PPP recognition events are driven by the interaction of hydrophobic SLiM residues that bind deep hydrophobic pockets on the PPPs.
source: Crystal structures of ordered SLiMs in complex with PPPs show that these recognition events are, in most cases, driven by the interaction of hydrophobic SLiM residues that bind deep hydrophobic pockets on the PPPs (Peti et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Peti et al., 2013.

claim: Single SLiMs typically bind to their cognate PPPs with moderate affinities.
source: Single SLiMs typically bind to their cognate PPPs with moderate affinities (Li et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2007.

claim: The existence of multiple SLiMs within a single regulator/substrate, coupled with post-translational modifications like phosphorylation, can greatly alter their affinity for their respective PPP.
source: However, the existence of multiple SLiMs within a single regulator/substrate, coupled with post-translational modifications like phosphorylation, can greatly alter their affinity for their respective PPP (Bajaj et al., 2018; Grigoriu et al., 2013; Kumar et al., 2016; Nasa et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bajaj et al., 2018; Grigoriu et al., 2013; Kumar et al., 2016; Nasa et al., 2018.

claim: IDPs can form high affinity complexes that are dynamic, in which the IDPs simultaneously retain their intrinsic structural disorder.
source: More recently, it has been discovered that IDPs can also form high affinity complexes that are dynamic; that is, in which the IDPs simultaneously retain their intrinsic structural disorder (Borgia et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Borgia et al., 2018.

claim: Dynamic IDP binding is typically driven by electrostatics.
source: In these cases, binding is typically driven by electrostatics (Borgia et al., 2018; Hendus-Altenburger et al., 2019; Luo et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Borgia et al., 2018; Hendus-Altenburger et al., 2019; Luo et al., 2016.

claim: The LxxIxE motif is the first PP2A:B56 specific SLiM.
source: Recently, the first PP2A:B56 specific SLiM, the LxxIxE motif, was identified (Hertz et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hertz et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2017.

claim: Proteins containing validated LxxIxE motifs bind B56 in a deep, highly conserved hydrophobic pocket.
source: Proteins containing validated LxxIxE motifs bind B56, an all α-helical heat repeat protein, in a deep, highly conserved hydrophobic pocket.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the manuscript.

claim: Most LxxIxE motifs bind PP2A:B56 with moderate affinities (low micromolar KD).
source: Most LxxIxE motifs bind PP2A:B56 with moderate affinities (low micromolar KD), similar to those observed for other PPP-specific SLiMs.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the manuscript.

claim: For PP1 and CN, enhanced affinities are achieved by exploiting avidity through regulators and substrates containing two or more distinct SLiMs.
source: However, for PP1 and CN, enhanced affinities are achieved by exploiting avidity; namely, regulators and substrates contain two or more distinct SLiMs which, together, result in tight affinities for their cognate PPP (Choy et al., 2014; Grigoriu et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Choy et al., 2014; Grigoriu et al., 2013.

claim: The residues that comprise the concave surface of B56 are exceptionally conserved.
source: An analysis of the amino acid conservation among 150 distinct B56 sequences shows that the residues that comprise the concave surface of B56 are exceptionally conserved (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence conservation analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: A surface adjacent to the LxxIxE pocket on B56 is highly negatively charged.
source: An examination of the electrostatic potential of the same region led to the identification of a surface adjacent to the LxxIxE pocket that is not hydrophobic, but instead is highly negatively charged (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrostatic potential analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The negatively charged surface on B56 is defined by multiple acidic residues that are perfectly conserved in B56.
source: This surface is defined by multiple acidic residues that are perfectly conserved in B56, both among its various isoforms and throughout evolution (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by conservation analysis shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: A subset of LxxIxE-containing B56 interactors including KIF4A, RepoMan (CDCA2), NHS and AIM1 are regulated specifically by the acidic patch for B56 binding.
source: The MS analysis shows that a subset of the LxxIxE-containing B56 interactors are regulated specifically by the acidic patch for B56 binding in both isoforms. This includes the mitotic regulators KIF4A, RepoMan (CDCA2), Nance-Horan syndrome protein (NHS) and absent in melanoma 1 protein (AIM1), (ratio WT/2R > 9, p-value<0.05; Figure 1D,E, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1D,E.

claim: The perturbation of interactions between the acidic patch and B56 interactors is not sufficient to perturb B56 function in supporting mitotic timing in HeLa cells.
source: While the perturbation of these interactions is not sufficient to perturb B56 function in supporting mitotic timing in HeLa cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B,C), it does reveal that the B56 acidic patch is a key binding determinant for a subset of LxxIxE containing PP2A-B56 interactors (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B,C.

claim: A conserved basic charged rich region exists within ~15 amino acid N-terminal to an established LxxIxE motif in KIF4A, RepoMan, NHS and AIM1.
source: Analysis of the primary sequences of these regulators highlighted the presence of a conserved basic charged rich region within ~15 amino acid N-terminal to an established LxxIxE motif, which we defined as a basic patch (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mutating the KIF4A basic patch (bpm, basic patch mutant: 1208KKK1210 to AAA) reduced the affinity of KIF4A1192-1232 for B56γ by ~4 fold.
source: The data showed that mutating the KIF4A basic patch (bpm, basic patch mutant: 1208KKK1210 to AAA) reduced the affinity of KIF4A1192-1232 for B56γ by ~4 fold (Figure 2B,C,D, Table 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data shown in Figure 2B,C,D, Table 1, and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Mutating the basic patch motif of RepoMan, NHS and AIM1 resulted in statistically significant reduced affinities for B56.
source: Similarly statistically significant reduced affinities were observed when the basic patch motif of RepoMan, NHS and AIM1 were mutated (CDCA2/RepoMan 563RKKK566 to AAAA; NHS 1618RCR1620 to ACA; AIM1 716KRKKAR721 to AAAAAA; Table 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 2C–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data shown in Table 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C–H.

claim: Only WT KIF4A co-purified efficiently with B56α, while basic patch mutant and I1227A mutant did not.
source: Although all three KIF4A variants (wt, bpm and I1227A) expressed to similar levels, only the WT KIF4A co-purified efficiently with B56α (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The basic patch motif contributes significantly to B56 binding for a subset of PP2A-B56 interactors.
source: Together, these data show that, for a subset of PP2A-B56 interactors, the basic patch motif contributes significantly to B56 binding.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented.

claim: The KIF4A LxxIxE motif peptide (CSPIEEEAH) binds B56 weakly (KD, 32 μM).
source: The KIF4A LxxIxE motif peptide (CSPIEEEAH), like that of Emi2, was previously shown to bind B56 weakly (KD, 32 μM) (Hertz et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hertz et al., 2016.

claim: The affinity of KIF4A1192-1232,LE for B56γ increased 50-fold compared to WT KIF4A (KD of 0.32 μM).
source: The affinity of KIF4A1192-1232,LE for B56γ increased 50-fold compared to WT KIF4A (Table 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 2I; KD of 0.32 μM).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data shown in Table 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2I.

claim: Mutating KIF4ALE residues 1231AH1232 to PE (KIF4ALE,PE) further enhanced KIF4A binding (KD of 0.10 µM).
source: Mutating KIF4ALE residues 1231AH1232 to PE (KIF4ALE,PE: the 'P, Pro' positions the 'E, Glu' to form a bidentate salt bridge with B56γ R201 Wang et al., 2016) further enhanced KIF4A binding (KD of 0.10 µM; Table 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 2J).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data shown in Table 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2J.

claim: Mutating the KIF4ALE,PE basic patch (1208KKK1210 to AAA) reduced the binding affinity by ~2 fold (KD of 0.22 µM).
source: Mutating the KIF4ALE,PE basic patch (1208KKK1210 to AAA) again reduced the binding affinity by ~2 fold (KD of 0.22 µM; Table 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 2K), a reduction similar to that observed for WT KIF4A (Table 1, Figure 2B,C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data shown in Table 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2K.

claim: The basic patch, together with the LxxIxE motif, are critical for a subset of regulators, including KIF4A, to stably interact with B56, independent of the strength of the LxxIxE motif.
source: Together, these data show that the basic patch, together with the LxxIxE motif, are critical for a subset of regulators, including KIF4A, to stably interact with B56, independent of the strength of the LxxIxE motif.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented.

claim: KIF4A residues 1207 to 1232, which includes the basic patch and the LxxIxE motif, were broadened beyond detection upon binding B56γ.
source: Specifically, KIF4A residues 1207 to 1232, which includes the basic patch and the LxxIxE motif, were broadened beyond detection upon binding B56γ.
evidence: This is a direct statement describing NMR spectroscopy results.

claim: In the crystal structure of the KIF4A1192-1232,LEPE:B56γ complex, while the LxxIxE motif is well-ordered, electron density corresponding to a single conformation of the basic patch bound to B56 was not observed.
source: A crystal structure of the KIF4A1192-1232,LEPE:B56γ complex (Figure 3—figure supplement 1; Table 2) showed that while the LxxIxE motif is well-ordered, electron density corresponding to a single conformation of the basic patch bound to B56 was, as expected, not observed.
evidence: This claim is supported by crystallographic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Table 2.

claim: In the crystal structure of the AIM1716-741:B56γ complex, while the AIM1 LxxIxE motif was well-ordered, electron density corresponding to a single conformation of the basic patch bound to B56 was not observed.
source: A crystal structure of the AIM1716-741:B56γ complex (Figure 3—figure supplement 1; Table 2) was similar. Namely, while the AIM1 LxxIxE motif was well-ordered, electron density corresponding to a single conformation of the basic patch bound to B56 was not observed.
evidence: This claim is supported by crystallographic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Table 2.

claim: The KIF4A basic patch binds B56γ via dynamic, rapidly interchanging conformations even when bound to B56.
source: Together, these data, coupled with the ITC results, show that the KIF4A basic patch interaction with B56 belongs to an emerging class of biomolecular complexes in which one or more partners of the complex retains their structural disorder upon complex binding. That is, the basic charged patch of KIF4A binds B56γ but does so via dynamic, rapidly interchanging conformations even when bound to B56.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on NMR and crystallographic data.

claim: The peaks corresponding to the KIF4A basic patch residues are present only with B56 variants with mutated acidic patch residues.
source: The NMR data showed that the peaks corresponding to the KIF4A basic patch residues are present only with B56 variants with mutated acidic patch residues (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR data shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: KIF4A binds the B56γ acidic patch variants more weakly than wild-type B56γ.
source: Consistent with these results, ITC showed that KIF4A binds the B56γ acidic patch variants more weakly (Table 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 2L,M).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data shown in Table 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2L,M.

claim: Mutating only E310R/D313R in B56γ was sufficient to reduce the binding affinity to the same extent as mutating the basic patch in KIF4A.
source: Interestingly, mutating only E310R/D313R was sufficient to reduce the binding affinity to the same extent as mutating the basic patch in KIF4A (KD: 0.19 ± 0.01 μM and 0.21 ± 0.01 μM for B56γ2R:KIF4ALEPE, and B56γ:KIF4ALEPE,bpm, respectively, Table 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 2L); additional mutations (i.e., E276R/E310R/D313R) did not further affect the binding (Table 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 2M).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data shown in Table 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2L,M.

claim: The binding of KIF4A and other bp-containing B56 interactors to B56 in cells was dependent on both an intact acidic patch in B56 and an intact basic patch in KIF4A.
source: In agreement with this result, we found that the binding of KIF4A and other bp-containing B56 interactors to B56 in cells was dependent on both an intact acidic patch in B56 (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 3) and an intact basic patch in KIF4A, as even single amino acid substitutions in the KIF4A basic patch lowered binding (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 3, and Figure 3F.

claim: The KIF4A basic patch interacts directly with the B56 conserved acidic patch and this interaction is critical for KIF4A binding.
source: Together, these data show that the KIF4A basic patch interacts directly with the B56 conserved acidic patch and this interaction is critical for KIF4A binding.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented.

claim: The observed phosphorylation level of KIF4A T799 was inversely correlated with affinities of PP2A-B56 for the different KIF4A variants in mitotic cells.
source: Strikingly, the observed phosphorylation level of T799 was inversely correlated with affinities of PP2A-B56 for the different KIF4A variants in mitotic cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Mutating either the LxxIxE motif (I1227A) or the basic patch (1209KKK1211 to AAA) resulted in an increase of phosphorylation of KIF4A T799.
source: Specifically, mutating either the LxxIxE motif (I1227A) or the basic patch (1209KKK1211 to AAA) resulted in an increase of phosphorylation of T799, as less PP2A-B56 was recruited to counteract the activity of Aurora B kinase.
evidence: This is a direct statement describing experimental results.

claim: The dephosphorylation of KIF4A T779 by PP2A-B56 requires the basic patch as the PP2A-B56 dephosphorylation efficacy is directly correlated with PP2A-B56 affinity.
source: Together, these data show that the dephosphorylation of KIF4A T779 by PP2A-B56 requires the basic patch as the PP2A-B56 dephosphorylation efficacy is directly correlated with PP2A-B56 affinity.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Depleting both KIF4A and hKid resulted in a strong mitotic delay, with multiple unaligned chromosomes.
source: Depleting both KIF4A and hKid resulted in a strong mitotic delay, with multiple unaligned chromosomes.
evidence: This is a direct statement describing experimental results.

claim: The mitotic delay phenotype from KIF4A and hKid depletion was fully rescued by complementation with WT YFP-KIF4A.
source: As expected, this phenotype was fully rescued by complementation with WT YFP-KIF4A.
evidence: This is a direct statement describing experimental results.

claim: Mutating the basic patch (bpm) resulted in a non-functional KIF4A that failed to localize to mitotic chromosomes.
source: However, mutating the basic patch (bpm) resulted in a non-functional KIF4A and this variant failed to localize to mitotic chromosomes (Figure 4C, bottom panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The defect in KIF4A function due to the bpm was not due to a lack of PP2A-B56 binding, as evidenced by the I1127A variant fully rescuing both the mitotic timing and the chromosome alignment phenotypes.
source: Further analysis revealed that this defect in KIF4A function due to the bpm was not due to a lack of PP2A-B56 binding, as evidenced by the observation that the I1127A variant fully rescued both the mitotic timing and the chromosome alignment phenotypes (Figure 4C, middle panel, Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4D.

claim: The abundance of all components of the condensin I complex were strongly reduced in the KIF4A bpm variant.
source: These data showed that the abundance of all components of the condensin I complex were strongly reduced in the KIF4A bpm variant (Figure 4E, Figure 4—source data 1), data that are consistent with the observation that this variant does not localize to chromosomes (Figure 4C, bottom panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The abundance of the components of the condensin I complex with the I1227A variant was unaffected.
source: In contrast, the abundance of the components of the condensin I complex with the I1227A variant was unaffected, consistent with the ability of this variant to properly target chromosomes during mitosis (Figure 4C, middle panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The basic patch targets KIF4A to chromosomes by binding condensin I.
source: These data confirm that the basic patch has a second, independent function; namely, it targets KIF4A to chromosomes by binding condensin I.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Both condensin I and PP2A-B56 binding strictly require the basic patch, so KIF4A cannot bind both proteins simultaneously.
source: Because we show that both condensin I and PP2A-B56 binding strictly require the basic patch, KIF4A cannot bind both proteins simultaneously, that is, condensin I and PP2A-B56 binding by KIF4A is mutually exclusive (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data presented.

claim: The novel dynamic, charge-charge interaction significantly contributes to understanding the diversity of mechanisms used by PP2A-B56 to select its substrates.
source: Here we describe a novel dynamic, charge-charge interaction for a major protein phosphatase, PP2A-B56, which significantly contributes to our understanding of the diversity of mechanisms used by this phosphatase to select its substrates.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the manuscript's findings.

claim: The novel interaction is mediated by a patch of basic residues that dynamically bind a highly conserved acidic surface present on all B56 isoforms and therefore constitutes a novel pan PP2A-B56 binding motif.
source: This novel interaction is mediated by a patch of basic residues that dynamically bind a highly conserved acidic surface present on all B56 isoforms and therefore constitutes a novel pan PP2A-B56 binding motif (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a summary statement of the manuscript's findings, supported by Figure 5.

claim: Charge-charge interactions are generally weak (low µM to mM).
source: Charge-charge interactions are generally weak (low µM to mM), yet are becoming increasingly recognized for their importance in increasing the binding affinity of protein:protein interactions, in part by lowering entropy (Bertran et al., 2019; Borgia et al., 2018; Luo et al., 2016; Sharma et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bertran et al., 2019; Borgia et al., 2018; Luo et al., 2016; Sharma et al., 2015.

claim: The unrelated B55 subunit also recognizes basic stretches of residues in substrates.
source: For example, the unrelated B55 subunit also recognizes basic stretches of residues in substrates (Cundell et al., 2016) but clearly the substrates for PP2A-B55 and PP2A-B56 are distinct.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cundell et al., 2016.

claim: The substrates for PP2A-B55 and PP2A-B56 are distinct.
source: For example, the unrelated B55 subunit also recognizes basic stretches of residues in substrates (Cundell et al., 2016) but clearly the substrates for PP2A-B55 and PP2A-B56 are distinct.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the manuscript.

claim: The binding affinity provided by the basic patch motif is insufficient for B56 binding and requires the presence of an LxxIxE motif.
source: In the case of PP2A-B56 the binding affinity provided by the basic patch motif is insufficient for B56 binding and requires the presence of an LxxIxE motif, which is specific for B56, in the interactor as well.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data presented.

claim: The function of the dynamic basic patch is to modulate and enhance the interactions mediated by the LxxIxE motif.
source: Thus, the function of the dynamic basic patch is to modulate and enhance the interactions mediated by the LxxIxE motif.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data presented.

claim: The basic patch may facilitate LxxIxE binding by providing an initial docking interaction after which the stronger LxxIxE stabilizes substrate binding.
source: It may also facilitate LxxIxE binding by providing an initial docking interaction after which the stronger LxxIxE stabilizes substrate binding; this is consistent with the view that long-range dynamic electrostatic interactions may function as an initial 'tether', after which the specific hydrophobic interactions that, in this case, define the LxxIxE-B56 complex, stabilize binding (Borgia et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by a citation to Borgia et al., 2018.

claim: The presence and contribution of the basic patch is important for a number of interaction partners to bind PP2A-B56.
source: Finally, we show that the presence and contribution of the basic patch is important for a number of interaction partners to bind PP2A-B56 underscoring its relevance and generality.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the manuscript's findings.

claim: The basic patch motif is strictly required for KIF4A association with chromatin via condensin I binding.
source: In the case of KIF4A, we also show that the basic patch motif has a second function. Namely, it is strictly required for KIF4A association with chromatin via condensin I binding;see also Poser et al. (2019).
evidence: This is a direct statement describing experimental results, with a citation to Poser et al. (2019).

claim: Because both KIF4A functions, binding to PP2A-B56 and condensin, strictly require the basic patch, the binding of both proteins to KIF4A is mutually exclusive.
source: Because both KIF4A functions, binding to PP2A-B56 and condensin, strictly require the basic patch, the binding of both proteins to KIF4A is mutually exclusive.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data presented.

claim: KIF4A only binds PP2A-B56 upon dissociation from chromosomes, consistent with the reported function of the KIF4A-PP2A-B56 complex in regulating the anaphase central spindle.
source: This implies that KIF4A only binds PP2A-B56 upon dissociation from chromosomes, consistent with the reported function of the KIF4A-PP2A-B56 complex in regulating the anaphase central spindle (Bastos et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data presented, supported by a citation to Bastos et al., 2014.

claim: Basic patch motifs resemble nuclear localization motifs (NLSs) recognized by importin α/β.
source: Since basic patch motifs resemble nuclear localization motifs (NLSs) recognized by importin α/β, the basic patch motifs would also be inaccessible for PP2A-B56 binding during nuclear transport (Lange et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lange et al., 2007.

claim: The accessibility of basic patch motifs provide an additional layer of regulation that shapes the PP2A-B56 interaction and dephosphorylation landscape in cells.
source: Thus, the accessibility of basic patch motifs provide an additional layer of regulation that shapes the PP2A-B56 interaction and dephosphorylation landscape in cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data presented.
